paragraphs.text: Once again Jewish wickedness wages war against the Lord's authority. Once again the folly of his opponents grows bold against the Savior's wisdom. Once again Jews contradict the Savior, both the old ones and the new: the old are those who crucified his body, the new are those who have sharpened their tongues against his Godhead. The first nailed the Lord's body to the cross; the second have nailed his uncreated nature to a creature. Yet if the two wickednesses are set side by side, the evils of the Jews are the more bearable. For it is one thing to tear a royal robe, and quite another to insult the King of glory himself.

The Jews marveled at the Savior, wondering how he knew letters when he had never studied. They did not say, "He does not know"; they marveled at how he knew letters without having learned them. They admit that he knows; the heretics deny that he knows. Blessed David refuted them when he bore witness to the Savior's knowledge of things past and of things to come: "You have known all things on earth, the last and the ancient." But what does the heretic say? He was speaking of the Savior when he said, "You have known all things on earth, the last and the ancient." But look at what follows: "You formed me and laid your hand upon me."

The heretics too admit that in this way all things belong to the Godhead, not that the Son is the whole as regards power, but as regards person [?]. For they cannot do away with him who truly is. Hear Paul saying: "If we deny him, he remains faithful; he cannot deny himself." But those who denied the Father were cut off from life in shame. They came to be outside the light; they were deprived of the living spring. And to those who are of two minds about his Godhead he cries out today and always: "If anyone thirsts, let him come to me." Who are you, then, that we who thirst should come to you? "I am the one to whom the prophets cried: O God, my God, I rise early to seek you; my soul has thirsted for you, for God the mighty." "If anyone thirsts, let him come to me."

And when does he say this? "On the last day, the great day of the feast" of the Jews. For the Savior's coming, being the last, put a limit to the things of the Jews. It gave a beginning to the things of the Gospel; it closed off the old and brought in the new. That is why Scripture, wishing to show at the Savior's resurrection how the old is dissolved while the new flowers and advances into beauty, says: "He rose late on the sabbaths." For that sabbath put an end to all sabbaths. "Late on the sabbaths": that sabbath was the end of the sabbaths.

It did not say "as the first day of the week followed," but "as it was dawning." It shows the light of the sabbaths. For the resurrection, or rather the death of Christ, is sung among the Jews as a death, but among the Gentiles the light of the resurrection shines out. That is why the Old Testament too divides the working of his very death. For the prophet says in his person: "Behold, I have set you as a testament for the race, as a light for the Gentiles." "Testament" is a word that implies death; "light" signifies the resurrection. Since, then, death is sung among the Jews while the resurrection is proclaimed among the Gentiles, the prophet anticipated this and divided the meaning of the saying, fitting the testament to the race, that is, the Jewish race, and joining the light to the Gentiles.

"Whoever believes in me, as the Scripture has said, out of his belly will flow rivers of living water." Many demand that we produce the testimony and show where it is written that whoever believes in Christ, rivers of living water will flow out of his belly. For the Savior said, "Whoever believes in me, as the Scripture has said, out of his belly will flow rivers of living water," not because this exact saying is written, but because it follows as a consequence for the one who believes: rivers of living water out of his belly. What are these rivers? The operations of the Spirit, the working of the adorable Spirit. There is one river, but many streams branch off from it. Just as a river goes out of paradise in Eden and is divided into four heads, so there is one river and one spring of life, but from it come forth the rivers of theology, the branches of the teaching.

Do you want to see rivers of living water flowing? Look at Paul, watering the whole world under heaven with holy rivers, from Jerusalem round about as far as Illyricum. He could never have been enough to water so vast a world if he had not had the working of the Holy Spirit overflowing within him. And truly he showed by the facts themselves that rivers of living water will flow out of his belly.

That by "rivers of living water" he meant the operations of the holy and adorable Spirit is shown by what follows. For the Gospel adds: "Now this he said about the Spirit, whom those who believed were to receive." Is the Holy Spirit, then, living water? Pay close attention. The Holy Spirit is living water. So if you hear God saying, "They have forsaken me, the spring of living water," understand God to be the spring of the Spirit. "They have forsaken me, the spring of living water." And the living water is the Holy Spirit. Therefore God is the spring of the Holy Spirit, a spring that pours forth from itself and brings forth from itself the Holy Spirit, a spring proclaimed by faith, not by comprehension. "For the heavens declare the glory of God." Not by comprehension. Hear what the prophet says: "His excellence covered the heavens, and the earth is full of his praise." Of praise, not of comprehension. Of faith, not of inquiry. They were baptized believing.

"Many of the crowd heard what he was saying. They said: This is truly the Prophet." "A prophet" would be something else. For the article, when added, indicates an authority that is proper and unique. Let me give an example, drawing my proofs from things worn smooth in common usage. If someone says, "A bishop has arrived," he has indicated the rank but has not identified the man. But if he says, "The bishop of the city," you recognize the one everyone talks about. Likewise, if you say "a doctor," you have indicated the profession but not identified the man; but if you say "the doctor," you are speaking of the one everyone knows. They did not say, "This man is a prophet," but "This is the Prophet." Which one? The acknowledged one, of whom it was said to you: "God has promised to raise up a prophet like me from among your brothers."

"Others said: This is the Christ." Here again pay attention to the article. "A christ" would be something else. For there are many christs, many anointed ones; priests too are anointed. But the Christ is one alone, and all have become partakers of him. That is why the prophet David said: "I am a partaker with all who fear you and keep your commandments." And the blessed prophet, showing that many became partakers of Christ in name, that many even became christs, many sharing the title without sharing the dignity, said: "Therefore God, your God, has anointed you with the oil of gladness above your partakers." He calls "partakers of Christ" those who have shared his title. So too Paul, understanding the sharing of the title, says on account of the title: "We have all become partakers of Christ, if we hold the beginning of our confidence firm to the end." For just as Christ, being the spring of good things, is partaken of by the worthy, so too the adorable Spirit is shared by the worthy. For the apostle says: "Those who were once enlightened, who tasted the word and became partakers of the Holy Spirit." Do you see how the Godhead is a participation in the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit? So they said, "This is the Christ." What folly! They divided what is one [?]. For the Prophet too is divided by different titles but joined in a single meaning.

Others said today: "Surely the Christ does not come from Galilee? Has not the Scripture said that he comes from the seed of David and from Bethlehem, the village?" Mark how the household rages against itself. Now the Jew, wishing to rule out his coming from Galilee, brings Bethlehem forward as proof. This is what he says: "The Christ is not from Galilee, because the prophet said: From Bethlehem, the village."

Then how does he say in another place, "We do not know where the Christ comes from"? See how wickedness is divided against itself, and how, as David said, "iniquity has lied." "When the Christ comes, we do not know where he comes from." Yet he says, "Is it not from the seed of David and from Bethlehem, the village?" Do you not realize that you are claiming knowledge? And if you know, why do you pretend not to?
"So there was a division in the crowd." They were split both in their souls and in their words, as David said: "They were split apart and were not pierced with compunction."

"Some of them wanted to seize him, but no one laid hands on him." Where his authority does not permit, wickedness has no power. Where his power does not yield, the scheming of those who try achieves nothing. They wanted to, but they did not succeed. For the Savior was keeping the right moment for his passion, he who keeps the truth in step with the type. He knew the day on which the type of the passion took place, and on that day the truth of the passion had to be fulfilled. Do you want to learn that his power conquers all things and is not overpowered unless it wills? They wanted to do away with him, but they were struck with darkness. They wanted to seize him in another place, in the temple, "and Jesus went out through the midst of them, hiding himself." If he went through the midst of them, how was he hiding himself?

He could have overthrown those ungrateful men with a single word. It was out of love for humankind that he bore the passion on the cross. He says to them, "Whom are you seeking?" They answer him, "Jesus the Nazarene." He says, "I am he." And they all fell backward. A single word overthrew them; it was not a threat that overthrew them. That is why the apostle, that noble herald of the truth, the chosen vessel, who had Christ speaking within him, knowing the sovereign authority of his power, and knowing that it was not wickedness that overcame [?] his power but his dignity that stooped down in love for humankind, says: "And he gave himself up for us."

"The officers came to the chief priests and the Pharisees, and they said to them: Why did you not bring him?" Notice here how wickedness is overthrown by itself. The chief priests sent officers to bring the Savior. The officers, struck numb by his divine teaching, came back, not as men defeated, but as men contending for the Savior himself.

"Why did you not bring him?" They say: "No one ever spoke like this man." See what a change the excellence of his teaching brings about. He received those who came to make war on him and made them friends. They came as enemies shooting arrows, and they were sent back as envoys pleading his cause.

"The Pharisees answered: Have you too been led astray? Has any of the rulers or of the Pharisees believed in him? Only this crowd, which does not know the law." Do you see how wickedness blinds? No one, they say, has believed in him, only the crowd that does not know the law. They cloak their own wickedness, as if it were their knowledge of the law that made them flee the teaching of Christ.

Does the law, Jew, train you to disobey Christ and to blame the crowd for believing, as though ignorant of the law? Indeed it is a marvel that those who did not know the law found the Lawgiver, and those who had not read the prophets found the one the prophets foretold. But you, who read the law, did you not recognize the one the law proclaims? Do you not know the law? Have you not understood the law? Did the law not say: "A ruler shall not fail from Judah, nor a leader, until there comes that which is laid up, and he is the expectation of the nations"? It set a boundary for the truth. It fixed piety unshakably in facts. Scripture prophesies concerning the coming of Christ that the kings of the Jews cannot possibly cease until Christ comes. Either, then, show that the Jewish kingdom still remains, and that Christ has not yet come; or, if you cannot show it, receive the one who has come. "A ruler shall not fail from Judah, nor a leader, until there comes that which is laid up, and he is the expectation of the nations." Very well: suppose the expectation of the nations has not come. How then did it flower? The farmer never came, yet the crops sprang up? The expectation of the nations never came, yet the nations worshiped?

But many twist this text with sophistries. The rulers of the Jews have not failed, they say; the patriarchs of the royal line of David remain. Well did Christ, the spring of wisdom, say: "Search the Scriptures." Under the law no one becomes king and ruler unless he is anointed. Succession does not make a king unless the horn of oil anoints the king. King David, wishing to install his successor, was not content with succession within the family. He summoned the prophet: "Take for me the boy Solomon. Let Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet take him, bring him down to Siloam, and anoint him." Do you see that succession does not make a king unless the anointing confirms the kingship? But pay attention to the precision of Scripture. The prophet, wishing to show how the land of Judea has been stripped of its rulers, says: "The children of Israel shall sit for many days with no ruler, no king, and no prophets." Even if you point to a ruler, if you cannot point to a prophet, does the truth lie? Do you see how, since they cannot establish their point, the way is shut against the opponents on every side? For it is not a title that makes authority; it is God's confirmation that ratifies authority.

"Nicodemus, who had come to Christ by night, says to them." Notice how the man who had never before spoken boldly takes his own timid disposition in hand, pricked by the Lord's words that "everyone who does evil hates the light and does not come to the light." Wishing to shake off the danger of that earlier night, he speaks boldly by day and undoes his denial by confession: "Does our law judge a man unless it first hears from him?" He called for a hearing for the Savior, knowing that the voice of God, once it came forth, could quench the sin and the madness of his opponents.

"They answered: Are you also one of his disciples? Search and see that no prophet has arisen from Galilee." Notice here, I beg you, the obstinacy of the Jews, and how the Savior's rebuke muzzles wickedness. "No prophet," they say, "has arisen from Galilee."

And what does the evangelist say? "Jesus cried out: I am the light of the world." What connection does this saying have with their denial? They say, "No prophet has arisen from Galilee." The Savior replies, "I am the light." What do the two sayings have in common? Why did he say, "I am the light"? Because they had dismissed Galilee as incapable of receiving the luminary of the world, he says, "I am the light," the light of which the prophet cried out: "Land of Zebulun, land of Naphtali, the way of the sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles: the people sitting in darkness have seen a great light." The prophet says that the light shines in Galilee, and you have ruled out Galilee as unable to bring forth a shoot of piety? "I am the light of the world." The Jews heard and wept. "When you turn back and groan, then you will be saved."

Turn the weapons of unrighteousness, heretic, into weapons that fight for piety. Become a champion of the truth. Imitate Paul, who was bold against Christ and afterward took up arms for Christ. For God always loves to seize the weapons of wickedness and make them weapons of righteousness. So it was once with Moses, whom he armed in the house of Pharaoh: he took the one believed to be the princess's son and sent him to campaign against that kingdom. So too God took Paul, who was fighting for the Jews, and armed him against the Jews. He was persecuting the Savior, and receiving all at once the working of the Spirit, he loved the one he had persecuted.

But you do not want to imitate Paul and Moses? Then imitate Nebuchadnezzar. Do not be more savage than the barbarian. That barbarian once, drunk with arrogance, not knowing the King of all and thinking himself master of nature, tried to compel those made in the image of God to worship his own image. When the three holy youths refused, those witnesses of the Holy Trinity, sheltered by the Holy Trinity, when they refused, the Babylonian says: "If you do not worship" (to cut the story short) "that very hour you will be thrown into the furnace of burning fire; and who is the god who will deliver you?"

Did you see the madness of a drunken barbarian? Did you see the madness of a man shooting arrows at God? Did you see how the creature did not know the Master who formed it? Did you see how the chaff contends against the fire? Did you see how the grass makes war on the flame? But he said these things in ignorance of divine power. And what does he do in his rage? "Heat the furnace sevenfold." Because the martyrs had said, "There is a God who is able to deliver us," he increases the punishment. And yet, most lawless tyrant, if there is no power of God, why do you needlessly multiply the flame sevenfold? Even an ordinary flame can consume a body. Why, then, sevenfold? It was so that he might defeat the promise of divine power by a contest of fire that he heated the furnace sevenfold.

But the word shone out, and the saying of the prophet David was fulfilled: "The words of the Lord are pure words, silver tried in the fire, proved for the earth, purified sevenfold." They shook off the flame, and the fire, like a bridal canopy, covered the bodies of the saints. The power of God made the furnace a church and turned the punishment into a feast. In place of laments it made hymns, and in place of flame, dew.

The tyrant says: "Shadrach, Meshach, Abednego, servants of the Most High God." Now you confess the Most High? Now you proclaim as God the one you denied a little while ago? Were you not the one saying, "And who is the god who will deliver you out of my hands?" Then say, you too, with Paul: "I acted in ignorance, in unbelief." And notice here how the weapon of wickedness was turned to the service of virtue. For he writes: "I write to tribes and tongues: whoever speaks a word against the God of Shadrach, Meshach, Abednego shall go to destruction, and their houses shall be laid waste." The one who threatened piety now contends for the truth.

So, heretic, more savage than Nebuchadnezzar, do not blaspheme the adorable Spirit. Do not blaspheme the Son by the very words with which you blaspheme the Spirit. Do not insult the Spirit by the very words with which you insult the Son. Do not insult the Father by the words with which you deny the root [?]. One spring, one life: whoever denies a part has denied the whole.

And what need is there to split hairs over the divine names: one holy Son from God? Son from God, and God. The how of it, faith hands down; human beings do not comprehend it. The resurrection, however, is a gift of God. Pay close attention: the resurrection is a gift of God. Of the resurrection Paul says: "If the dead are not raised, then Christ has not been raised either; your faith is futile." Whoever denies the resurrection will have a futile faith. Does someone who asks in the name of the Trinity have an uncertain benefit?

Do you not know that the prophets are instruments of the Holy Spirit? Do you not know that the apostles were sent by the Holy Spirit? He says to the apostles: "I too send you into the world." If it is Christ who sends, then the Holy Spirit is claiming the Son's authority for itself. For the Holy Spirit says at Antioch, the great city: "Set apart for me Paul and Barnabas for the work to which I have called them." If it were a servant, it ought to have acknowledged its subordinate role and said, "for the work to which Jesus has called them"; but instead it claimed the royal authority for itself: "Set apart for me Paul and Barnabas for the work to which I have called them." And indeed the prophet says that those called are called by God, since "from Zion will come the one who is saved and the one who brings good news, whom the Lord has called" [?]. How then does the Holy Spirit say, "for the work to which I have called them"? "For the Lord is the Spirit," says Paul, "and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom."

But enough of these matters. There is one thing, however, that has struck my soul, which I am ashamed to speak of and yet compelled to speak of. Some of the godless heretics, having no way to wound the ears of the church by their own audacity, dare to circulate the sayings of the pagans and to repeat them as true. The ears that would not receive these words were wounded, not harmed, but stricken for the sake of those who are scandalized. I am compelled to repeat what I heard, to refute those who dare to say it, to strengthen those who hear, and to defend the truth. Not that the truth needs our defense; but we must help him who helps all, we must help God when he is slandered. Do not seize on the phrase and object, "Help God?" I am following Scripture. The blessed Deborah, that prophetess, says that those who did not join the war against the foreigners are accursed, those who did not come out to help the Lord.

Many of the heretics, then, throw against us sayings put about by pagans. And what does one of the pagans say? The wickedness of the heretics hides its own weapons, since it has been defeated with them, and brings out borrowed ones, to shake the foundations of piety. Some of the pagans have said: "Ever since Christianity, there have been wars. Ever since the idols were overthrown," they say, "the world has been overthrown." Forgive me, I beg you, for using what our opponents put forward as material for my proof. The truth would be enough on its own, contending for itself. But one must take the weapons of the enemy and cut them down with those weapons oneself. So blessed David, when he had overcome his adversary with a sling and had no means of cutting off his head, took the enemy's own sword and cut off the enemy's head.

"Since the idols were overthrown, there have been wars." Well then: when Xerxes came to Athens and burned it, and razed all Achaea and Greece to the ground, did they not have gods? Did they not have altars? Did they not have mystery rites? Did they not have sacred blood? If war comes because the idols were overthrown, why was there war back then, when Hellenic religion was at its height? When cities fought against cities, when villages made war on villages, when every hand went about with a sword, when no one could travel in peace, when no one could go along any road at all [?] without a sword, where were the idols then? I am ashamed to be speaking on behalf of idols. I defile my tongue in order to refute the defiled. Read the Roman histories. Read about the ancient wars. Read about the ancient evils: the wars Thucydides wrote about, the ruin of the Peloponnese, the destruction of all Greece. Read about the Assyrians who said: "Where are your gods, Thamar and Ashur? Have your gods been able to save their own land?" But the impious man takes advantage of people's ignorance of ancient times, and he muddies it with the present condition of humanity as it appears to them.

Since Christ came, local war has ceased, and war with foreign peoples is fading away. Back then it was city against city, nation against nation. Now the very word "war" alarms you, because you have grown so used to peace. Once you came to know peace, you forgot the vocabulary of war. For the prophet said: "They shall beat their swords into plowshares and their spears into sickles, and they shall never again learn to make war."

Next he says: "So after Christ is adultery not practiced?" For that is what they bring up. "So after Christ is fornication not practiced?" After Christ, lust came to be recognized as fornication. Back then it was held in honor. Read the ancient laws, or rather the ancient myths. Look at the evils of the Greeks. A woman who fornicated was called a goddess. She was an adulteress, yet she was given the name of goddess. And the so-called father of the gods, with the evils by which he changed himself into countless forms of licentiousness, was so far from being recognized as a fornicator that he was even worshiped as a god.

But now that the ray of chastity has shone, it has been shown what fornication is and what purity is. The light has revealed what is honorable, and what is honorable has shone out. Being used to evil, though, kept you from even noticing the evil. It is like this (to use a common saying: it is only a human expression, but I will use it anyway). Those who live in a tannery do not notice the stench because they are used to it, and in the same way being used to evil made people numb to it. Now that purity has shone, that is, Christ, the rays of holiness, fornication is shown up as fornication. For think, brothers, of a man wearing dirty clothes. Wherever he sits, in whatever filth, nothing shows on him. (For his state had already been [?], and nobody reproaches him for sitting anywhere at all and keeping company with dirt. The dirt that is already there does not show up any more dirt. But if someone puts on a bright robe, then whatever happens to fall on it shows up as something foreign.) In the same way the world back then was filthy, wearing a filthy garment. Wallowing in evils, it was not shown up. But when the light of Christ shone, the great extent of fornication came into view. This is not because there is as much of it as there was then. It is because now it cannot be hidden.

Look at the devil's malice and what he devised for the ancients. The devil is a craftsman, grown old in evil days. He knew that people differ in character and that they are not all moved by the same habits. One is chaste by nature, another licentious by habit. One has a weakness for bloodshed, another for anger and rage. Wanting to master every passion and strike down everyone, he set up idols of various kinds. What does licentious fornication, graceless adultery, say? "Do not think that adultery is evil. Look at Adonis. Look at the so-called Cyprian. The gods you worship commit fornication, and you are ashamed to commit adultery? None of those you worship feels shame, and you, the worshiper, feel ashame?" He saw the licentious and set up wretched [models] of licentiousness for them. He saw the chaste and devised a counter-scheme for them. What does he say? "Do you long for chastity? You have Artemis, you have Athena. They are virgins. They do not want marriage." So whether you want chastity or licentiousness, you can have it freely and without fear. The devil wanted to bind every art, every pursuit and every way of life to godlessness, so he devised a patron figure for every activity. Are you a craftsman? Honor Hephaestus. Are you a vinedresser? Honor Dionysus. Do you long for the bosom of the earth? Honor Demeter. This is what Paul spoke of. Paul saw that God's gifts were being worshiped while God himself was unknown, and so he says: "They exchanged the glory of God and served the creature rather than the Creator." Are you a hunter? You have Artemis the huntress. Let no one think the teaching is defiled if we name Artemis or Dionysus. The holy Scriptures too record what the Greeks said: they called Barnabas Zeus and Paul Hermes. Since these were the names, you have seized on them, enemy of the truth. You cover up the ancient evils and pin all that confusion of evils on the truth, and then you dare to say that since the light shone the darkness has increased?

But perhaps they object: "If those things were evil and base, and these things bright and saving, why are there wars?" Why? Because the greed that is idolatry is with us now. Paul spoke of it: "and greed, which is idolatry." Do you want to learn why there are wars, why cities are made desolate, why a land that had many men is reduced to a few? Hear the prophet: "Hear the word of the Lord, house of Jacob, for the Lord has a case against the inhabitants of the land. Therefore there is no mercy of the Lord and no knowledge of him. Cursing and lying and theft and adultery are poured out over the land. They mingle blood upon blood. Therefore the land shall be diminished, together with all who live in it." This is why cities and houses are made desolate: because your houses have no walls [?]. This is why wars kindle walls like fire: because justice has been despised, the poor are trampled and the arrogant are honored. These words are not mine, even if some people are indignant. Are they not true? Tell me, blessed prophet, why the fire, why the earthquake, why the destruction? "I will send fire upon the walls of Teman, and it shall devour the walls of Jerusalem." Why? "Because they struck the heads of the poor with their fists, and took away the right of the righteous, and sold the needy for a pair of sandals." Therefore the Lord will bring this wrath, and the rulers will perish. Why? Because of their undisciplined tongue. Do you see a fire being kindled and still add wood to it? This is why the markets in the city have been deserted: because the signs [?] were not honored in the markets. This is why houses have been shut up: in truth, truth shuts up its own house [?]. Why will you not live in your own house and enjoy your own things? Because you seek what is not your own. That is why the prophet says: "Because you struck the head of the poor with your fists and took choice gifts from them, therefore you have built fine houses, and no one will live in them. You have planted vineyards, and you shall not drink their wine. You have oil, and you shall not anoint yourselves with it."

"But then, Lord, you have shown the wound without applying the treatment." For there are souls in need of treatment. You have seen the nature of the wound; see the power of the remedies. Strip off injustice through righteousness. Strip off robbery through love of the poor. Strip off blasphemy through singing hymns. Undo evil things with good things. Set their opposites against base deeds.

Many people say: "What am I to do? How shall I prevail on God?" Look at how the prophet too refutes people in distress. He says to them: "With what shall I come before the Lord?" He brings on a character who is at a loss and looking for a way to serve God. "With what shall I come before the Lord and lay hold of God Most High? Shall I appease him with tens of thousands of fat lambs? Shall I give my firstborn for the sin of my soul?" He is saying: how am I to serve God with sacrifices, and offer my children as offerings for myself?

Then God exposes the fabricated pretense and refutes it at once: "Has it not been told you, O man, what is good, and what God requires of you?" Do not say, "What am I to do?" For you know, and you do not do it. Heal the wound. Hear the prophet saying: "Gather together and be bound together, undisciplined nation, before the wrath of the Lord comes upon you." Let them entreat the Lord, in case he may be merciful toward their sins. The threat is fearful, but repentance is strong. The judge is fearful, but the advocate is strong. Repentance knows how to restrain the judge. It knows how to throw its arms around him. It knows how to say, "And I pardon." Already God accepts it, even as a just judge. Prevail on him through prayer. Bring martyrs, apostles and prophets before him, to see whether they can persuade him. This is how God wants to be held back, wants to be reconciled, wants to be prevailed upon. "Come to him and be enlightened." Do not say: "Many have prayed; what came of the prayers?" God answers you: "Is my hand too weak to deliver? Or has my ear grown too dull to hear? Your sins stand between me and you."

We say these things to heal, not to wound. Let us entreat God, brothers. When he is angry he wants to be held back. When in his anger he wants to be reconciled, he pretends to be refusing his own loving-kindness. He says to Moses: "Let me alone, so that I may wipe out this nation." What a hint of loving-kindness in the guise of a threat! "Let me alone" in place of "Hold me back"! Moses heard one thing and did another. He heard "Let me alone" and took "Let me alone" to mean "Hold me back." Being wise, he understood: "God says 'Let me alone' to me as though I were able to restrain him. So if through some negligence I do not restrain him, then 'Let me alone, and I will wipe out the nation.' And what are you doing for me? 'I will make you into another great nation.' If I do not keep the first nation in faith, how will the second trust me? 'Let me alone.'" As soon as he heard "Let me alone," he was fired up to "Hold me back," says the Lord [?]. Now pay close attention here. We must accept advice even from someone lesser and inferior. A man gives advice to God: "And if you kill them, the nations will say: 'Because the Lord was not able to give them the land he promised, he killed them in the wilderness.'" Then, even if he grieved them before the nations [?]: "What grieves me is not that the people should fall, but that you should be blasphemed." See how the wise servant defends the nation in the guise of one fighting for his master: "I am grieved that you may be blasphemed. The people deserves to fall, but you do not deserve to be blasphemed. 'Because the Lord was not able to give them the land, he killed them.'" And what will you do for your great name? That is, "What can we do when your glory is insulted?" God accepts the advice (this is why he became angry in the first place, to give boldness to the advice), and says: "And now I am merciful, according to your word. But as I live, and as my name lives." And how is the Son's name the Father's? Hear him saying: "I have come in my Father's name, and you did not receive me." "But as I live, and as my name lives": both for the sake of the name of Christ and for the sake of the glory of my Church, by which God swears. Hear the prophet saying: "The Lord swears by his holy ones."

Still, these things have been said to us so that you may learn that God wants to be held back. Let us restrain him, not with our hands but with prayers, not with mere confessions but with works of righteousness. Since you cannot cry out very much yourself, hire the poor to cry out for you.

I know how to linger over a speech and not linger over a grievous misfortune [?]. Prepare in advance how you will persuade the judge, so that you may prevail on the magistrate. He is ready for those who are willing. "The Lord is near to all who call upon him in truth." Rather, do not ask why there is war; keep silent and make your defense [?]. Do not say, "Why these things?" Say instead, as a believer, "Why only these things?" And yet you examine God's judgment and say, "Why did God bring war upon us?" Have you ever seen a condemned man receive an explanation from the judge? The condemned man has only one concern: to make his own defense. You are liable for countless sins, and you demand an explanation from the judge? Are you so fond of lawsuits [?] that you would question him about the cause of what happens? Are you righteous, that you should demand an explanation? That is why God complains: "They seek me day after day and long to know my ways, as though they were a people that had done righteousness." You are answerable for so many sins, and you demand an explanation from the judge? What need is there to fight, not with God but with ourselves? Do you see a fire being kindled and still kindle his wrath? Quench it with prayer. Bring dew against the fire. Wrath is fire; prayer is dew.

But this is enough. Anyone who is not moved to shame by a part will not be moved by the whole either. Let us be afraid, brothers, I beg you. Strange reports are reaching us from every side. The reports are many, but there is One who is stronger than them all. God can be content with the report, and discipline us by what we hear and by what we experience. If you repent, God says about us: "I discipline them by the report of their affliction."

May we make our defense to the judge in word, conduct and life, and having emptied many [?], so that many tears may be poured out [?]. And so, by the prayers of the holy apostles and the holy martyrs who poured out their blood for Christ, may the conflagration be quenched. May our pious emperor be shown to be the victor and be armed with divine weapons. May one soldier be sent from heaven to the emperor (for one soldier is enough), to come and fill [?] the city. For the multitude of the Assyrians was great, yet one angel in one night struck down a hundred and eighty-five thousand. If we live soberly, God says about us: "And you, keep still."

Grant, Lord, that the emperor may be crowned and shown to be the victor, that the barbarians may be destroyed, that the cities may be made firm, and that the blood of the saints that has been shed may quench the conflagration. Then may we all sing hymns in peace to the Master of peace, to whom be glory with peace for ever and ever. Amen.
